newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close lower in thin trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Sunday on very low volume as investors remained on the sidelines, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.21 percent, or 0.52 points, to 242.43 on all-share turnover of 53 million shekels against 164 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.29 percent lower at 250.16.

"Trading was very dull today. The market was mixed and trendless," said Eyal Kolka of Sigma Securities. "The fact that the market has traded in a very narrow range during the last 10 days shows that the outlook is positive."

"The fact that there's no trading on Wall Street until Tuesday adds to the uncertainty, but the Maof has found strong support at 250. We believe that if the political situation improves the market will start rising. Right now investors are sitting on the fence," Kolka said.
But other analysts were less bullish, citing concerns about the future of the peace process.
On Sunday, clashes continued for the 11th straight day in the West Bank as Palestinians protested Israeli construction in Arab East Jerusalem.
"Investors are waiting to see where the peace process is going. They do not want to take any risks and prefer to wait for further developments," said Noam Braverman at the Central Securities Corp.
The only positive factor today was that the market did not react to the Dow's decline on Thursday, Braverman added.
Israel Corp fell 2.0 percent to 22,504 agorot and Israel Chemicals, the third most active share, fell 1.75 percent to 355 agorot on turnover of 1.9 million shekels.

Israel Corp's chairman and controlling shareholder Shoul Eisenberg died last Thursday in Beijing after suffering a heart attack. On Sunday, the company purchased 17 percent of Israel Chemicals from the government, paying 667 million shekels in cash.
The purchase raised its stake in Israel Chemicals to 41.5 percent.
Shekem rose 3.25 percent to 123 agorot. The company reported a fourth-quarter net profit of 13 million shekels against a year-earlier net loss of 13 million shekels.
Mofet Israel Technology Fund gained 1.0 percent to 163 agorot. Mofet reported a fourth-quarter net profit of 596,000 shekels against net loss of 2.26 million shekels a year earlier.

The most active shares were Clal Israel, which rose 2.5 percent to 93 agorot on turnover of 3.1 million shekels, and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 2.0 percent to 880 agorot on volume of 2.8 million shekels.
